steps.what: the carrier is ORIENTATION-PURE: 06.1's even permutations (sign +1) are closed under composition; 2I subset SU(2) = proper rotations (det +1)
steps.why: the handedness, sitting in plain sight in 06. Container 06.1 is literally 'the even permutations of four coordinates', and its own note records that 'taking the odd orbit instead gives a conjugate copy' -- the carrier is one orbit, the EVEN one. Even permutations have sign +1 (orientation-preserving); the sign is a homomorphism to {+1,-1}, so a product of even permutations is even -- the 12 even permutations (A4) are closed under composition. RUN IT: |EVEN| = 12, and even.even = even for all pairs. So nothing the carrier does reverses orientation. This matches the quaternionic picture: 2I is a finite subgroup of SU(2), and SU(2) double-covers SO(3) = the PROPER rotations (det +1); there is no reflection (det -1, an improper element) anywhere in the carrier. The carrier is orientation-PURE -- one handedness, built in.

steps.determines: UNIQUE (parity sends the even carrier to the disjoint odd conjugate copy -- not a self-map)
steps.expr: an orientation reversal is an ODD permutation / a reflection (sign -1). Composing it with any carrier (even) element gives an ODD map (odd.even=odd) -- it lands in the OTHER orbit, the conjugate (odd) copy, which is a DISTINCT carrier (06 finding-2 / CORRECTIONS #5), disjoint from the even one. So the mirror image of the carrier is NOT the carrier: the substrate is CHIRAL

steps.what: PARITY is not a self-symmetry: an orientation reversal carries the carrier to the DISTINCT conjugate (mirror) copy
steps.why: the chirality itself: the carrier is not equal to its own mirror image. Parity (a reflection, an orientation reversal) is an ODD permutation, sign -1. Apply it to the carrier's even orbit: odd.even = odd (the sign flips), so every carrier element is sent OUT of the even orbit into the odd one. The odd orbit is the CONJUGATE copy of the carrier -- 06's finding 2 / CORRECTIONS #5: the base (0,1/2,phi^-1/2,phi/2) on the even orbit vs the odd orbit are conjugate copies differing in 96 of 120 elements, the same abstract 2I in a mirror embedding. The two orbits are DISJOINT (a permutation is even or odd, never both). So parity maps the carrier to a DIFFERENT carrier -- it is not a self-symmetry. The substrate has a definite HANDEDNESS. (This is why 06 had to CHOOSE the even orbit and record the odd as the conjugate: the choice IS the chirality.)
